Part C · Poetry: Paraphrase & the Turn

4 Questions ·

Read the poem, then answer E1–E4. You may revise all four responses until you submit this passage set. Choose what the words support, not just what sounds positive.

The Unfinished Kite

1I bent the reeds to match my plan,2then pressed the paper flat and tight.3Each loosened edge I sealed again;4no seam would spoil its maiden flight.

5Outside, it dragged across the stones.6I watched the careful corners fold.7My sister held the tangled string:8“The frame needs room for wind to hold.”

9We freed a corner from its tape.10The kite rose crooked, dipped, then stayed.11I let the pencil leave my hand12and watched the shape the breezes made.

Original poem written for this homework.

E1. Which sentence most accurately paraphrases the first stanza? L2

E2. Which pair best describes the speaker’s change in attitude from the first stanza to the last? L3

E3. Which line first shows the speaker acting on a less rigid approach? L3

E4. How does “crooked” in line 10 contribute to the poem’s meaning? L4

Answer every question, audit, then submit the set.

Part D · Poetry: Tone & Evidence

4 Questions ·

Read the poem, then answer E5–E8. You may revise all four responses until you submit this passage set. Choose what the words support, not just what sounds positive.

Before the Street Wakes

1The shutters guard their darkened squares;2the bus stop holds a single chair.3I stand beside my heavy bag4and count the windows, dim and bare.

5Then wheels begin beneath the bridge;6a baker lifts a silver tray.7An upstairs window opens wide;8a radio unwinds the day.

9The street has kept its cracks and stains.10My bag still pulls against my knee.11I shift to make a stranger room;12the waking city waits with me.

Original poem written for this homework.

E5. Which sentence best paraphrases the second stanza? L2

E6. Which pair best describes the shift in the speaker’s attitude? L3

E7. Which detail most strongly supports the answer that the speaker’s stance toward others has changed? L3

E8. Why does the poet state that the street still has “cracks and stains” and the bag is still heavy? L4

Part E · Poetry: Images & Transfer

4 Questions ·

Read the poem, then answer E9–E12. You may revise all four responses until you submit this passage set. Choose what the words support, not just what sounds positive.

After the Last Bell

1We stacked the chairs against the wall,2and folded maps along their seams.3The empty hooks, the silent clock:4the room seemed smaller than our dreams.

5I reached to wipe the board quite clean,6then stopped beside a crooked line:7a route we drew and drew again,8with arrows crossing yours and mine.

9I left one arrow on the board10and took the chalk beyond the door.11The hallway had no lines to follow;12my hand could still imagine more.

Original poem written for this homework.

E9. Which sentence most accurately paraphrases the first stanza? L2

E10. Where does the poem first signal a possible turn away from simply clearing the room? L3

E11. Which statement best describes the movement in tone across the poem? L3

E12. What does taking the chalk into the unmarked hallway most strongly suggest? L4

Answer every question, audit, then submit the set.
